text:
Morgan: Thanks for a packed all-hands. One recurring ask: can leadership map where we actually have a defensible edge vs competitors (hyperscalers + specialized inference vendors)? Looking for a simple gap analysis and the roadmap levers we can pull in the next 6 months.
Asha: Love this. Proposed quick framework: 1) Capability moat (features + integrations), 2) Economics moat (unit cost + predictability), 3) Ops moat (onboarding, reliability, legal). We'll populate a 2x2 with customer pain points.
Riley: For GTM, we need one-liners for each quadrant. Marketing can't lead with vague "best-in-class" claims.
Priya: Field report: customers care most about predictable bills and migration risk. If we solve billing transparency + migration tooling we close a lot of mid-market deals.
Diego: Engineering notes: short term wins we can ship: better KV cache warmup, more aggressive prefix reuse, and a small SDK that emulates vendor X's streaming API to make migrations seamless. Low dev effort, big UX win.
Zoe: Data point: in last 20 pilot accounts, average token spend dropped 18% after we enabled prefix caching. I'll add a short analysis to the shared drive.
Sam: Prioritization ask: which of these should hit the roadmap this quarter vs Q2? We need triage so teams can sprint.
Asha: Proposal: Q1 focus = migration friction (adapters + migration checklist) + billing clarity (per-route cost breakdown). Q2 focus = performance knobs in Redwood Optimize + public benchmarks.
Evan: Legal caveat: for migration adapters, ensure we don't ship anything that implies compatibility with proprietary SDKs. Keep wording neutral and provide mapping docs rather than "drop-in replacement" claims.
Priya: Also: Dedicated deals sometimes hinge on encryption and KMS controls. We should prioritize a one-page legal/tech brief for Sales to attach to RFPs.
Riley: Messaging tests: can we A/B two headlines on the website next week? Variant A: "Predictable unit economics for LLMs" Variant B: "Production latency and reliability for LLMs". Track trial signups and demo requests.
Morgan: Good. What measurable signals tell us were improving? Suggest 4 metrics: 1) percent of Dedicated evaluations that convert in 45d, 2) median p95 latency for new production routes, 3) reduction in billing-related N1 escalations, 4) # of migrations completed using our adapter.
Diego: I'll scope the adapter work and prefix improvements. Estimate: adapter MVP = 3 dev-weeks + 1 week QA. Prefix cache improvements = 2 sprints of infra work.
Zoe: I'll publish the pilot analysis and add a playbook entry showing token savings per workload type.
Asha: I'll draft the 6-month roadmap with clear milestones and owners. Will put a short version in Confluence and a ship checklist for each milestone.
Priya: I'll coordinate with Legal on the KMS/contract one-pager and share template language.
Riley: I'll run the A/B homepage experiment and report back.
InfraBot: Note: all-hands follow-up doc and roadmap sketch uploaded: https://confluence.redwood/ah/1749965432.
Morgan: Thanks team. Action owners: Asha (roadmap doc), Diego (adapter + prefix work), Zoe (pilot analysis), Priya (legal brief), Riley (homepage A/B). We'll reconvene in 10 days to review the draft roadmap and the experiment results. :spiral_calendar:
